questions.explanationHtml:
(a, b, c)
• For a number to be divisible by 3 and 9, the sum of its digits should be divisible by 3 and 9
respectively. Here, 1 + 2 + 3 + 7 + 5 = 18, which is divisible 3 and 9 both. Hence, the number is
divisible by both 3 and 9.
• For a number to be divisible by 11, the difference between the sum of digits in the odd
positions and even positions must be a multiple of 11 or 0. Here, (5 + 3 + 1) – (7 + 2) = 0. Hence,
the number is divisible by 11.

questions.questionMarkup: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding quicksand condition?
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding quicksand condition?

options.html: A soil becomes ‘quick’when the flow is upward under a hydraulic gradient which reduces the total stress to zero
options.text: A soil becomes ‘quick’when the flow is upward under a hydraulic gradient which reduces the total stress to zero

options.html: Human beings and animals are not sucked into a quicksand
options.text: Human beings and animals are not sucked into a quicksand

options.html: Quicksand condition mainly occurs in highly pervious sands
options.text: Quicksand condition mainly occurs in highly pervious sands

questions.explanationHtml:
(a, c)
Quicksand is simply sand saturated with water, which reduces friction between the sand particles
and makes the mixture behave like a fluid when disturbed. It can also be seen as a viscous fluid
with a unit weight twice that of water. Hence, any person can easily float in it, material being
viscous renders movement of body very tiring. But there is no development of negative pressure
or ‘sucking’ action in this phenomenon. In very pervious sands and gravels, the large discharge
required to maintain a quick condition make it improbable for its occurrence.

options.html: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid is used as the titrant in this method.
options.text: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid is used as the titrant in this method.

options.html: 1 ml of 0.01 M titrant measures 1 mg of hardness as CaCO<sub>3</sub>.
options.text: 1 ml of 0.01 M titrant measures 1 mg of hardness as CaCO 3 .

options.html: The colour change at the end point shifts from blue to red.
options.text: The colour change at the end point shifts from blue to red.

options.html: This test can only measure hardness due to Ca<sup>2+</sup> and Mg<sup>2+</sup> ions.
options.text: This test can only measure hardness due to Ca 2+ and Mg 2+ ions.

questions.explanationHtml:
(a, b, d)
Hardness can be measured directly by titration with ethylenediamine tetraacetic acid (EDTA)
using eriochrome black T (EBT) as an indicator. The EBT reacts with the divalent metallic cations,
forming a complex that is red in color. The EDTA replaces the EBT in the complex, and when the
replacement is complete, the solution changes its colour from red to blue. If 0.01 M EDTA is used,
1.0 mL of the titrant measures 1.0 mg of hardness as CaCO3.
